subject: Ouroborus cataphractus, the armadillo girdled lizard, biting its tail (Logan's confirmed subject, 2026-10-03)
what_the_eye_sees: Hero at 300 px: a scaled reptile coiled round the finger with its head at about 1 o'clock where the coil closes. The bite still reads: the tail thins down the right side and runs up into the jaws. But the new 'real limbs' do not show in this view. Nothing breaks the outer silhouette at 10-11 o'clock or 7-8 o'clock. There are only a few small pale pegs and nubs on the inner edge of the band at about 8 and 10 o'clock, and at this size they read as burrs or clasp parts, not as legs with elbows and feet. The head is still a boxy block with a comb of vertical spikes along its top and an eye socket in a square face, so it reads as a dragon or a crested serpent, not as a broad, flat lizard head. The body girdles are still even, square-topped blocks of nearly the same size all the way round, so the hide reads as crocodile or dragon armour. A jeweller without a caption would say 'dragon ouroboros' or 'snake ring'. Face at 300 px: this view still fails. The head from above is a shield or coffin shape tiled with kite plates. It is widest across the middle and blunt at both ends, with a fringe of spikes on each flank, so it does not taper to a snout. In front of it (left of frame) two pairs of thin, straight, diagonal struts stand out about 45 deg on either side. These are the new limbs, but they are pencil-thin, they have no elbow, no hand and no toes, and they meet the body at a squared collar block. They read as the legs of a bracket, a tripod or a beetle's legs, not as a lizard's forelegs gripping its flank. Beyond them the band ends in a squared, scaled cylinder at the frame edge, and on the right the body is a row of even ribs, like a spring. The overall impression is a beetle or a piece of hardware clamped on a ribbed rod. Nobody would name a lizard from these two views.

changes.what: Make the limbs read as limbs in both views. Today they are thin straight struts that show only in face view and vanish in the hero. Build each one as a thick upper arm and forearm with a clear elbow, ending in a broad hand with splayed toes clamped to the flank, and push it out far enough to break the hero silhouette.
changes.where: Foreleg parts just behind the head (theta about 125-145 deg) and hind-leg parts at the hips (theta about 230-250 deg), both side faces. In face-300 they are the diagonal struts to the left of the head; in hero-300 they should sit at about 11 o'clock and 8 o'clock.
changes.by_how_much: Thicken each limb to about 1.4-1.6 mm at the upper arm or thigh and 1.1-1.2 mm at the forearm or shin, which is roughly 3x today's strut. Bend it at a 70-100 deg elbow or knee that points outward and slightly back, so the elbow stands 1.0-1.5 mm proud of the side face. Keep the 45 deg splay in plan, but make the limb rise up over the band's shoulder, not run flat in the plane of the crown, so that it shows on the outline in the hero. End it in a hand or foot of 4-5 toes, each at least 0.5 mm thick, splayed across a 2.0-2.5 mm span and gripping the flank, with the claws curling back onto the side face. Delete the squared collar block the struts spring from, and blend the shoulders into the body with a fillet. Acceptance: in hero-300 a bent foreleg with a visible splayed hand breaks the outer outline next to the head, and a hind leg does the same at about 8 o'clock. In face-300 each side shows an elbow and a splayed hand, and nobody would call them struts or a bracket.

changes.what: Make the head a lizard's head in plan: a triangle widest at the back and narrowing to the snout. Today it is a coffin-shaped shield, widest in the middle and blunt at both ends, with a spike comb along the top.
changes.where: Lizard head part, theta about 93-125 deg: the crown plates, both flanks, and the vertical spike comb on the crown visible in hero-300
changes.by_how_much: Taper the flanks in straight lines from about 1.35x the band at the back of the head (the occipital line, about 120 deg) to about 0.45-0.5x the band at the snout (about 93 deg), so the snout is under 40% of the back width and the head is about 1.4x as long as it is wide. Move the spiny occipital scales to the back edge of the head as 3-4 spines pointing back and outward that break the outline by 0.4-0.6 mm. Remove the comb of vertical spikes along the crown, and cut its height by at least 40% so the head top reads flat. Put a domed eye bulge 0.3-0.4 mm proud of each flank at about 60% of the head length back from the snout, with a small ear pit behind it. Pinch the neck behind the occipitals to about 0.8x the head width. Acceptance: face-300 shows a flat wedge head, broad at the back and pointed at the snout, with eye bumps and a spiny back edge on its outline. Nobody would call it a shield, a coffin or a beetle.

changes.what: Make the girdles spiny and graded instead of square crenellations, and dress the bitten tail as a tail, not a spring.
changes.where: Girdle tiling, theta 125 deg through the palm to about 78 deg; the tail tip at 78-93 deg
changes.by_how_much: Round each girdle's flat top into a loaf with a radius of at least half its height. Raise the trailing-edge spines to 0.4-0.6 mm, pointing tailward, so the hero's outer edge bristles. Make the pitch fall visibly from 2.6 mm at the nape to 1.0 mm at the tail. On the last 15 deg of the tail, replace the even ribs with small overlapping scales with spines of 0.2 mm or less. Acceptance: in hero-300 the outer edge reads as a ring of spines rather than steps, and the scales visibly shrink toward the jaws. In face-300 the tail on the right no longer reads as a spring.
